blocks.text: How to reason about it

An operation budget translates a time limit into deliberately simplified units. One hash lookup, cache miss, allocation, comparison, interpreted-language step and vector instruction do not have equal wall-clock cost. Big-O also removes constants and lower-order terms. Therefore a claim such as 10^8 must name its abstract cost model and remain a first-pass filter, not a universal runtime guarantee.

Use the estimate to reject orders-of-magnitude mismatches. Near the boundary, benchmark the relevant implementation or preserve a conservative margin because the abstract units no longer decide the outcome.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

The phases run sequentially, so their costs add. Preprocessing contributes n log n once, while q queries contribute q · log n. The full dominant workload is therefore n log n + q log n = (n + q) log n under the shared logarithm. Looking only at one query understates repeated work; multiplying preprocessing by q overstates a phase performed once.

Write the lifecycle formula before substituting values: construction + updates + queries + mandatory output. Add sequential phases and multiply a per-operation term only by the number of times that phase executes.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

Big-O groups algorithms by long-run growth, not exact work. Two O(n) implementations may perform one comparison per element versus hashing, allocation and several random memory accesses; two O(n log n) sorts may have different constants and cache behavior. Growth class reliably rejects large-order mismatches, but near a tight limit these hidden factors can decide feasibility.
Use asymptotics first, then refine only surviving near-boundary candidates with operation mix, allocation, locality, language/runtime and representative measurement.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

If the contract requires k records, the system must at least visit or write those k outputs, establishing an Ω(k) time lower bound. Returning them simultaneously usually also needs Ω(k) output storage, or more when each record has nonconstant size. An internal search faster than k does not remove the cost of satisfying the external result contract.
Separate computation, emission and retention. Streaming can reduce peak output memory, but it cannot make producing k required records take o(k) time.

The table contains 50,000 · 50,000 = 2,500,000,000 cells. Even at an idealized one byte per boolean, that is about 2.5 GB before row objects, alignment and runtime overhead; wider boolean storage makes it larger. If the memory limit is below that footprint, the representation is rejected before transition speed matters.

Translate space formulas into bytes using the actual representation and include container overhead. A compressed bitset changes the constant substantially, but it must be an implemented representation rather than an assumed rescue.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

An honest estimate declares that its units abstract unequal real operations, preserves constant and cache uncertainty near the boundary, and checks memory plus mandatory output independently. It can justify rejecting a clearly oversized candidate or selecting one for measurement, but it cannot prove identical wall-clock time across languages, hardware and implementations.
State both the conclusion and its confidence boundary: decisive order-of-magnitude rejection, plausible with margin, or benchmark required.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

Separate the one-time construction P(n) from the per-query cost Q(n). Multiplying Q(n) by q captures all requested queries, after which P(n) + q·Q(n) can be compared with alternatives. Update maintenance, memory and output remain additional terms when the workload includes them.

Identify the cost Q(n) of one query under the maintained representation.
Multiply by the maximum query count to obtain q·Q(n).
Compare P(n) + q·Q(n), update work and memory with the full workload budget.

Substitution gives 30,000 · 30,000 = 900,000,000 dominant operations. Dividing by the 100,000,000-unit budget gives a factor of nine. Because the dominant count alone already overruns the budget, normal overhead only strengthens the rejection; a different algorithmic bound is required under this model.
A ninefold gap is more than a tiny boundary uncertainty, but the conclusion still belongs explicitly to the abstract unit model rather than universal wall-clock time.
